column3: Close to the Hebrew; “they seize [them]” is rendered “take them by violence.”
Close to the Hebrew; “this clan” is rendered “this family,” and “calamity” “disaster.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he will wail a wailing” is rendered “lament with a bitter lamentation,” and “an apostate” “a turncoat.”
Close to the Hebrew; “one who casts a measuring line by lot” is rendered “no one to determine boundaries by lot.”

NKJV renders “do not prophesy (drip)” as “Do not prattle,” supplies “you say” and “to you,” and renders “disgrace will not turn back” as “They shall not return insult for insult”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “is it said, O house of Jacob” is rendered “You who are named the house of Jacob,” and “is the Spirit short?” “Is the Spirit … restricted?”
Close to the Hebrew; “yesterday” is rendered “Lately,” and “from those who pass by securely” “From those who trust you, as they pass by”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “a grievous destruction” is rendered “with utter destruction.”
Close to the Hebrew; “walking [in] wind and falsehood” is rendered “walk in a false spirit,” and “the prophesier (dripper)” “the prattler.”

Close to the Hebrew; “like sheep of Bozrah (a sheepfold)” is rendered “like sheep of the fold,” and “they will be in uproar from [the] people” “They shall make a loud noise because of so many people.”
